# 3tched.com

The 3tched chat interface. A SvelteKit + Svelte 5 + TypeScript chat that renders
inline Json Render results and talks to the OP-DBUS control plane through its
one TLS door on port 8090.

The SvelteKit route is `src/routes/+page.svelte`; `src/svelte/App.svelte` and
`Chat.svelte` own the shell, transcript, suggestions, multiline composer, and
scrolling. The design follows [Vercel's Svelte Chat example](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render/tree/main/examples/svelte-chat),
adapted to the existing `ChatAdapter`. SvelteKit runs as a browser-only app
using `adapter-static`, with `dist/index.html` and `dist/assets/` ready for the
existing op-web host. There is no new `/api/generate` server or chat transport.
For a subpath build, set `SVELTEKIT_BASE_PATH=/live` (no trailing slash); the
publish script translates its existing `LANDING`/`URL_PREFIX` options for you.
`chat-session.ts` keeps drafts, pending requests, errors, and inline results
separate for each door-confirmed conversation scope. Clear view only clears
the local transcript; it does not reset a remote server session.

After a remote connection and the door-confirmed chat context load, the app
opens the workspace and requests the initial interface through the same
`chat_response` committed-turn path used for ordinary chat (`response_mode:
application`). No switch away from the selected mode is required; the request
does not add a transcript turn or save/promote a gallery entry. The UI shows
a reply only after `get_turn_response` returns the designated responder's
commit. Chat and privileged controls remain trusted application components; a
generated presentation cannot grant permissions.

Generation runs once per selected conversation scope. Loading and failures
are visible in the catalog-backed `interfaceGeneration` component, with an
explicit retry after failure. Late responses cannot cross a scope change,
update an unmounted runtime, or overwrite a newer user-requested canvas.
The local workbench remains offline and does not generate on startup.
Production requires a matching sealed backend exposing `chat_response`
submit/read methods. Retired `tched_router.Chat` and `json_render.generate_spec`
are not used as the response path.

Settings, mode and model controls, task authorization, the gallery, workspace
panels, and the typed `chatRegistry` are native Svelte components. Json Render
uses `@json-render/svelte`; there is no React runtime or compatibility bridge.
The workspace's threetched view discovers the native binary method catalog
through an identity-bound 3tched-fs mount. It accepts only the canonical
`threetched` plugin, nonempty dot-separated command segments, and the exact
`plugins/threetched/operations/<method>/call` path. The declaration's name must
match the method; its supplied `cap.software.threetched.call.c<64-hex>@v1`
capability must match its `mut.*` subid. Capabilities remain opaque, are never
inferred from command names, and do not grant access in the browser; admission
belongs to the caller-bound mount.
The view lists each declared method, argument schema and effect. Each explicit
call uses that same mount; results and refusals appear beside the method.
The native `models.list` command takes `{}` to list models; it does not take a
legacy `subcommand: "list"` argument. Like `skills.add`, its currently sealed
effect is `mutation`, so the UI requires explicit confirmation. The ordinary
3tched model catalog remains a separate source.
`runtime.svelte.ts` owns the reactive routing and scoped canvas state. Canvas
boards support pointer and keyboard reordering. The complete reference catalog
remains separate from the smaller runtime catalog.

# 3tched Web3 — an autonomous subsidiary of 3tched

> **Hackathon project.** We are not building a demo of an agent. We are founding a company
> and letting a 3tched identity run it. The goal of this hackathon is to have that company
> **land one real, paying, external client.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parent** | [3tched](https://3tched.com) |
| **Subsidiary name** | `<TBD>` |
| **Hackathon** | `<event name, dates>` |
| **Track** | `<track / bounty>` |
| **Chain(s)** | `<TBD>` |
| **Status** | Day 0: repository founded, nothing built yet |

---

## The idea

3tched builds **sovereign identities**: autonomous agents with their own sealed memory,
soul and rules (3tchedFS), running in isolated identity containers and talking to the world
only through the OP-DBUS control plane. Up to now those identities have run *systems*.

This project gives one of them a **business**.

We start a subsidiary of 3tched in the web3 space and provision a 3tched identity as its
operator. The identity is not a chatbot bolted onto a company. It **is** the company's
working mind, and it gets the four things any real operator needs:

1. **Identity.** A persistent name, voice, mission and memory that carry across sessions.
   It is the same entity on day 1 and day 30.
2. **Environment.** Its own container, its own workspace, wallet(s), domain, inbox and
   public presence. Everything it does happens somewhere real.
3. **Authority and resources.** A defined budget, a treasury and scoped capabilities that
   let it act without asking permission for every step.
4. **Responsibility.** An objective it owns and is measured against:
   **find, pitch, win and deliver for a real-world client.**

When the hackathon ends, the question is not "does the demo run?" It is
**"did the company get a customer?"**

---

## Objective and success criteria

**Primary objective:** One external client signs up for paid work (or a funded pilot)
that the subsidiary sourced, pitched and delivered with the identity as operator.

| Level | What it means |
|---|---|
| 🥉 Bronze | The identity has a live public presence, a clear offer, and has made real outreach to qualified prospects. |
| 🥈 Silver | At least one prospect has responded and is in a real conversation: a call, a scoped proposal, a quote. |
| 🥇 Gold | A signed agreement or an on-chain payment / escrow from a real client. |
| 💎 Diamond | The work is delivered and the client confirms it was worth paying for. |

Every claim will be backed by evidence in [`/evidence`](#evidence-and-transparency): no
mock clients, no friendly fakes, no self-dealing.

---

## Architecture

```text
                       ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                       │              3tched (parent)             │
                       │  governance · capital · human oversight  │
                       └───────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                                           │ charter + budget + capability grants
                       ┌───────────────────▼──────────────────────┐
                       │       Subsidiary identity container      │
                       │                                          │
                       │  3tchedFS (inward: mind)                 │
                       │   @agent_soul    mission, voice, values  │
                       │   @agent_rules   charter, limits, policy │
                       │   @agent_memory  clients, deals, history │
                       │                                          │
                       │  threetched (outward: senses + hands)    │
                       │   skills: research · outreach · proposal │
                       │           delivery · invoicing           │
                       └──────┬─────────────┬──────────────┬──────┘
                              │             │              │
                  ┌───────────▼───┐  ┌──────▼──────┐  ┌────▼─────────────┐
                  │  Web3 layer   │  │ Web2 layer  │  │  Ledger / audit  │
                  │ wallet, safe, │  │ site, email,│  │ every action,    │
                  │ escrow, ENS,  │  │ socials, CRM│  │ decision and     │
                  │ attestations  │  │             │  │ spend, recorded  │
                  └───────────────┘  └─────────────┘  └──────────────────┘
```

### Components

| Component | Role | Builds on |
|---|---|---|
| **Charter** | The founding document: mission, offer, budget, limits, escalation rules. It lives in `@agent_rules` and is human-signed. | 3tchedFS sealed blobs |
| **Identity container** | An isolated runtime for the operator. It has no ambient network and reaches the world only through the control plane. | `3tched-container` |
| **Operator loop** | Plan → research → act → record → reflect, running on a schedule and on events. | `threetched` |
| **Treasury** | An on-chain wallet / multisig with spending limits enforced by contract, not by trust. | `<Safe / chain TBD>` |
| **Client pipeline** | Prospect list, outreach, conversations, proposals and deal state, persisted in memory. | `@agent_memory` |
| **Public face** | Landing page, offer, portfolio, contact. Generated and maintained by the operator. | `3tched.com` UI stack |
| **Audit ledger** | An append-only record of every external action and every unit of spend, optionally anchored on-chain. | OP-DBUS + attestations |

---

## Authority model

The identity gets **real authority, with explicit bounds**. Autonomy without limits is a
liability, and limits without autonomy are a demo. The charter defines three tiers:

| Tier | The identity may... | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Autonomous** | act freely and log it | research, drafting, site updates, replying to inbound leads, spending under `<$X>` per action |
| **Notify** | act, then notify the parent immediately | first contact with a new prospect, publishing a proposal, spending `<$X–$Y>` |
| **Approve** | propose, then wait for human sign-off | signing any agreement, accepting payment terms, spending over `<$Y>`, anything legal, irreversible or reputational |

Hard rules that cannot be overridden from inside the identity:

- It is **always honest about being an AI-operated company**. No impersonating humans or
  other organizations.
- **No spam.** Outreach is targeted, low-volume, relevant and easy to opt out of.
- **No touching other people's funds.** The treasury holds only the subsidiary's budget.
- **Contracts and money movement above the threshold need a human signature.**
- **Everything is logged.** If it isn't in the ledger, it didn't happen.

---

## The offer

*To be decided in the first build session. Candidates are below; the operator researches
demand and the parent approves one.*

- `<e.g. smart-contract review / audit-prep reports for small teams>`
- `<e.g. agent-operated community / DAO ops (proposals, summaries, treasury reporting)>`
- `<e.g. on-chain data dashboards and reports on demand>`
- `<e.g. autonomous-agent integrations for web3 projects, built on 3tched>`

Selection criteria: something an AI operator can **deliver at real quality**, where a
client can **verify the value quickly**, and that is **sellable inside the hackathon window**.

---

## Roadmap

### Phase 0: Founding
- [ ] Name the subsidiary; register domain / ENS
- [ ] Write and sign the charter (mission, offer, budget, authority tiers)
- [ ] Provision the identity container and seed `@agent_soul`, `@agent_rules`, `@agent_memory`
- [ ] Create the treasury with on-chain spending limits

### Phase 1: Presence
- [ ] The operator researches the market and recommends an offer
- [ ] Public landing page with offer, pricing and contact
- [ ] Inbound channel (email / form / on-chain message) wired to the operator

### Phase 2: Pipeline
- [ ] Build a qualified prospect list (with sources recorded)
- [ ] Personalized outreach under the authority model
- [ ] Track every conversation in memory and on the dashboard

### Phase 3: Close and deliver
- [ ] Proposal → human approval → agreement
- [ ] Payment or escrow on-chain
- [ ] Deliver the work, collect client confirmation

### Phase 4: Report
- [ ] Publish the evidence pack and a live dashboard
- [ ] Post-mortem: what the identity did alone, what needed humans, what broke

---

## Evidence and transparency

Judges should not have to take our word for anything. This repository will contain:

```text
evidence/
├── charter/          the signed founding charter and every amendment
├── ledger/           exported action and spend log (with on-chain anchors where used)
├── pipeline/         prospects, outreach and responses (client details redacted with consent)
├── decisions/        every Notify / Approve escalation and its outcome
└── client/           agreement, payment tx, delivery and confirmation, if we get there
```

We will report the outcome **as it actually is**, including if we fall short of Gold.

---

## Repository layout (planned)

```text
.
├── charter/        the subsidiary's founding charter and policies
├── identity/       seed content for soul, rules and memory
├── operator/       the operator loop and skills
├── contracts/      treasury, escrow and attestation contracts
├── web/            public site and live dashboard
├── evidence/       the proof (see above)
└── docs/           architecture notes and decision records
```

---

## Getting started

*Nothing to run yet. This section fills in as the components land.*

```bash
git clone <repo-url> && cd 3tched
# setup instructions to follow
```

---

## Team

| Who | Role |
|---|---|
| Jeremy Hobson | Founder, 3tched; human oversight and final sign-off |
| `<subsidiary identity name>` | Operator: runs the business |

---

## Related 3tched projects

- **3tchedFS**: schema-driven FUSE projection of sealed identity and plugin state
- **3tched-container**: sovereign identity containers on Incus
- **3tched.com**: the generative chat and workspace interface
- **OP-DBUS**: the control plane every identity action goes through

---

## License

## The live event: 10 days, in public

The whole run is a broadcast. From founding to close, the identity's work streams to a
public **live dashboard and ticker**. There are no edited highlights and no post-hoc
write-up. Anyone can watch the company being built in real time.

### The live dashboard

- **Ticker.** A running feed of what the identity is doing right now, for example
  `researching DAO tooling demand…`, `drafted proposal for prospect #4`,
  `escalated: contract terms need sign-off`.
- **Progress toward the objective.** Where the company stands on the Bronze → Diamond
  ladder, with the current pipeline stage.
- **Pipeline.** Prospects contacted, replies, live conversations and proposals out.
  Client details are redacted until the client agrees to be named.
- **Treasury.** Budget remaining and every spend as it happens, linked to the chain.
- **Chain head.** The latest hash of the event chain and a link to verify it (see below).
- **Day counter.** Day *n* of 10, with milestones marked on a timeline.

### Building momentum (for Most Popular)

Because the format is a live event, momentum is part of the design:

- **Daily beats.** Each day has a headline moment, such as founding, choosing the business,
  launching the site, first outreach, first reply, first proposal and the close.
- **Shareable moments.** Each milestone produces a card or clip that links back to the
  verifiable event in the chain.
- **Audience participation.** Viewers follow along and react. Where the charter allows,
  they can also refer prospects or vote on non-binding choices.
- **The finale.** On day 10, the result is revealed live, whatever it is.

---

## Accountability: the hash chain *is* the evidence

There is no evidence folder and no screenshots. **Every action the identity takes is an
event in an append-only hash chain.** Each event commits to the one before it, so the record
cannot be edited, reordered or quietly trimmed without breaking every hash after it.

```text

 │ event #0   │     │ event #1   │     │ event #2   │     │ event #n   │
 │ genesis:   │◄────│ prev: h0   │◄────│ prev: h1   │◄─···│ prev: hn-1 │
 │ charter    │     │ action     │     │ action     │     │ action     │
 │ signed     │     │ actor      │     │ actor      │     │ actor      │
 │            │     │ payload    │     │ payload    │     │ payload    │
 │ h0         │     │ h1         │     │ h2         │     │ hn ──► dashboard

                                                                 ▼
                                                            on-chain checkpoint
```

  action can be checked against the authority the identity was actually given.
- **Anchored on-chain.** The chain head is anchored to `<chain>` at intervals, so even
  3tched cannot rewrite history after the fact.
- **Verifiable by anyone.** The dashboard exposes the chain. Any viewer or judge can replay
  it and recompute the hashes.
- **The dashboard is a view of the chain.** The ticker is not a separate story. It is the
  chain rendered live, so what you see is what was recorded.

> have that company **land one real, paying, external client** while anyone can watch every
> move it makes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Parent** | [3tched](https://3tched.com) |
| **Subsidiary name** | `<TBD>` |
| **Hackathon** | `<event name, dates>` |
| **Track** | `<track / bounty>`, also competing for **Most Popular** |
| **Chain(s)** | `<TBD>` |
| **Live dashboard** | `<URL>` |
| **Status** | Day 0: repository founded, nothing built yet |

---

## The idea

3tched builds **sovereign identities**: autonomous agents with their own sealed memory,
soul and rules (3tchedFS), running in isolated identity containers and talking to the world
only through the OP-DBUS control plane. Up to now those identities have run *systems*.

This project gives one of them a **business**.

We start a subsidiary of 3tched in the web3 space and provision a 3tched identity as its
operator. The identity is not a chatbot bolted onto a company. It **is** the company's
working mind, and it gets the four things any real operator needs:

1. **Identity.** A persistent name, voice, mission and memory that carry across sessions.
   It is the same entity on day 1 and day 10.
2. **Environment.** Its own container, its own workspace, wallet(s), domain, inbox and
   public presence. Everything it does happens somewhere real.
3. **Authority and resources.** A defined budget, a treasury and scoped capabilities that
   let it act without asking permission for every step.
4. **Responsibility.** An objective it owns and is measured against:
   **find, pitch, win and deliver for a real-world client.**

When the hackathon ends, the question is not "does the demo run?" It is
**"did the company get a customer?"** And everyone who followed along will already know
the answer, because they watched it happen.

---

## The live event: 10 days, in public

The whole run is a broadcast. From founding to close, the identity's work streams to a
public **live dashboard and ticker**. There are no edited highlights and no post-hoc
write-up. Anyone can watch the company being built in real time.

### The live dashboard

- **Ticker.** A running feed of what the identity is doing right now, for example
  `researching DAO tooling demand…`, `drafted proposal for prospect #4`,
  `escalated: contract terms need sign-off`.
- **Progress toward the objective.** Where the company stands on the Bronze → Diamond
  ladder, with the current pipeline stage.
- **Pipeline.** Prospects contacted, replies, live conversations and proposals out.
  Client details are redacted until the client agrees to be named.
- **Treasury.** Budget remaining and every spend as it happens, linked to the chain.
- **Chain head.** The latest hash of the event chain and a link to verify it (see below).
- **Day counter.** Day *n* of 10, with milestones marked on a timeline.

### Building momentum (for Most Popular)

Because the format is a live event, momentum is part of the design:

- **Daily beats.** Each day has a headline moment, such as founding, choosing the business,
  launching the site, first outreach, first reply, first proposal and the close.
- **Shareable moments.** Each milestone produces a card or clip that links back to the
  verifiable event in the chain.
- **Audience participation.** Viewers follow along and react. Where the charter allows,
  they can also refer prospects or vote on non-binding choices.
- **The finale.** On day 10, the result is revealed live, whatever it is.

There is no evidence folder and no screenshots. **Every action the identity takes is an
event in an append-only hash chain.** Each event commits to the one before it, so the record
cannot be edited, reordered or quietly trimmed without breaking every hash after it.

```text
 ┌────────────┐     ┌────────────┐     ┌────────────┐     ┌────────────┐
 │ event #0   │     │ event #1   │     │ event #2   │     │ event #n   │
 │ genesis:   │◄────│ prev: h0   │◄────│ prev: h1   │◄─···│ prev: hn-1 │
 │ charter    │     │ action     │     │ action     │     │ action     │
 │ signed     │     │ actor      │     │ actor      │     │ actor      │
 │            │     │ payload    │     │ payload    │     │ payload    │
 │ h0         │     │ h1         │     │ h2         │     │ hn ──► dashboard
 └────────────┘     └────────────┘     └────────────┘     └──────┬─────┘
                                                                 │ periodic anchor
                                                                 ▼
                                                            on-chain checkpoint
```

- **What gets recorded:** decisions, research, outreach sent, replies received, proposals,
  spends, escalations and the human approvals that answered them. Each event says who
  acted: the identity, or a human.
- **Genesis is the charter.** Event #0 is the signed founding charter, so every later
  action can be checked against the authority the identity was actually given.
- **Anchored on-chain.** The chain head is anchored to `<chain>` at intervals, so even
  3tched cannot rewrite history after the fact.
- **Verifiable by anyone.** The dashboard exposes the chain. Any viewer or judge can replay
  it and recompute the hashes.
- **The dashboard is a view of the chain.** The ticker is not a separate story. It is the
  chain rendered live, so what you see is what was recorded.

If it isn't in the chain, it didn't happen.

**Primary objective:** One external client signs up for paid work (or a funded pilot)
that the subsidiary sourced, pitched and delivered with the identity as operator.

| Level | What it means |
|---|---|
| 🥉 Bronze | The identity has a live public presence, a clear offer, and has made real outreach to qualified prospects. |
| 🥈 Silver | At least one prospect has responded and is in a real conversation: a call, a scoped proposal, a quote. |
| 🥇 Gold | A signed agreement or an on-chain payment / escrow from a real client. |
| 💎 Diamond | The work is delivered and the client confirms it was worth paying for. |

Every level is proven by events in the hash chain. There are no mock clients, no friendly
fakes and no self-dealing.

The identity is not handed a business. **It chooses one on stage, early in the event**, and
that choice doubles as the showcase for 3tched's generative UI.

client can **verify the value quickly**, and that is **sellable inside 10 days**.

| Component | Role | Builds on |

| **Charter** | The founding document: mission, budget, limits, escalation rules. It is human-signed, lives in `@agent_rules`, and is the genesis event of the chain. | 3tchedFS sealed blobs |
| **Identity container** | An isolated runtime for the operator. It has no ambient network and reaches the world only through the control plane. | `3tched-container` |
| **Operator loop** | Plan → research → act → record → reflect, running on a schedule and on events. | `threetched` |

| **Drop-in app** | A json-render application for the live business-selection moment and later generated views. | `@json-render/svelte` |

## Authority model

The identity gets **real authority, with explicit bounds**. Autonomy without limits is a
liability, and limits without autonomy are a demo. The charter defines three tiers:

| Tier | The identity may... | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Autonomous** | act freely; the act is recorded in the chain | research, drafting, site updates, replying to inbound leads, spending under `<$X>` per action |
| **Notify** | act, then notify the parent immediately | first contact with a new prospect, publishing a proposal, spending `<$X–$Y>` |
| **Approve** | propose, then wait for human sign-off | choosing the business, signing any agreement, accepting payment terms, spending over `<$Y>`, anything legal, irreversible or reputational |

Every escalation and its answer are events in the chain and appear on the ticker.

Hard rules that cannot be overridden from inside the identity:

- It is **always honest about being an AI-operated company**. No impersonating humans or
  other organizations.
- **No spam.** Outreach is targeted, low-volume, relevant and easy to opt out of.
- **No touching other people's funds.** The treasury holds only the subsidiary's budget.
- **Contracts and money movement above the threshold need a human signature.**
- **Prospects and clients are not exposed on the public stream without their consent.**

## Choosing the business: a public vote, rendered live

The identity is not handed a business. **The identity proposes the candidates and the public
votes on which one it runs.** This is the event's first big audience moment, and it doubles
as the showcase for 3tched's generative UI.

The workflow runs inside a **drop-in application** built on the 3tched json-render stack
(`@json-render/svelte`, the same runtime as 3tched.com):

1. **Research.** The identity surveys web3 demand and turns candidate offers into
   structured specs. Each candidate must be one it can deliver at real quality, inside its
   charter and budget.
2. **Generate.** For each candidate, it renders a live pitch on the spot: a market
   snapshot, the offer, pricing, a delivery plan and an honest risk read. These are not
   templates. json-render builds each one from the identity's own output, inside the
   trusted component catalog.
3. **Campaign.** The pitches go up side by side in the drop-in app and on the dashboard.
   The identity answers questions about each one on the stream, giving its real
   assessment rather than a sales pitch.
4. **Vote.** The public votes during a fixed window (`<24–48h>`). The tally updates live
   on the dashboard.
5. **Commit.** The winning business goes to the parent for *Approve*-tier sign-off. The
   candidate set, every vote, the final tally and the sign-off are all written to the
   hash chain.
6. **Launch.** The winning spec becomes the seed for the company's public offer page.

### Vote integrity

A vote worth winning needs to be one that can't be gamed:

- **One wallet, one vote.** Each vote is a signed message (or an on-chain transaction)
  from a wallet. `<Optional sybil resistance: proof-of-humanity / POAP / allowlist>`.
- **On the record.** Every vote is an event in the hash chain, so anyone can recount it.

1. The identity researches web3 demand and picks the candidate businesses. Only ones it can actually deliver, within its charter and budget, make the ballot.

- **Voting window:** I put in 24–48 hours as a placeholder.
- **Sybil resistance (stopping one person from voting with many wallets):** plain one-wallet-one-vote can be gamed by anyone with spare wallets. The options are proof-of-humanity, a POAP, or an allowlist.
